display.purpose: Headlines only: hero title, ticket title, menu item names, closing headline.

label.purpose: All uppercase wide-tracked microcopy: category headers, captions, CTA text, prices, stamp text.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy: menu item descriptions, closing paragraph.

shadows.name: ingredient-cast
shadows.purpose: Applied to every floating/assembling ingredient image and the assembled burger photo for consistent physical-object lighting.

shadows.name: ticket-panel-lift
shadows.purpose: Menu ticket panel only; contact shadow plus soft ambient cast shadow.

motion.name: hero-scroll-assembly
motion.value: GSAP timeline pinned to ScrollTrigger, start 'top top', end '+=125%', scrub 1, stagger 0.075s per layer, ease power2.inOut
motion.purpose: Drives the burger-layer scroll-assembly sequence in the hero.

motion.name: float-idle
motion.value: gsap.to loop, y +/-12px, x +/-6px, duration 2.2-3.5s, sine.inOut, yoyo
motion.purpose: Idle float applied to each ingredient before scroll assembly begins.

motion.name: reveal-standard
motion.value: autoAlpha/y fromTo, duration 0.6-0.9s, power2.out, ScrollTrigger start 'top 65%-70%', toggleActions play none none reverse
motion.purpose: Standard section-enter reveal used by menu ticket and closing section content.

components.name: Section Checker Strip

components.css: .ds-checker-strip { width: 100%; height: 12px; background-image: conic-gradient(#211a13 0.25turn, transparent 0.25turn 0.5turn, #211a13 0.5turn 0.75turn, transparent 0.75turn); background-size: 16px 16px; }

narrative.overview: Fliiping Burgers stages a burger's construction as an event rather than showing the finished product. The system carries one continuous material story across three acts: a dark stage where loose ingredients float and assemble on scroll, a cream diner-ticket paper where the assembled burger anchors a printed menu, and a warm in-restaurant photograph that closes the page. Vintage American diner ephemera — condensed poster display type, checkerboard trim, torn paper edges, a hand-drawn stamp badge — is the connective tissue that makes the three acts read as one world, not three unrelated sections. The palette is deliberately staged rather than uniform: each section owns its own dark-to-warm register (near-black stage, cream paper, amber-lit restaurant), unified only by the diner-red accent and the checkerboard motif that repeats at the top of every section. This is a brief-pinned world (menu-card-inspo.png, full-food-footer-image-inspo.png) — no open-ended exploration was run, so its diner vocabulary is treated as load-bearing, not decorative.
keyCharacteristics: Three-act color staging (dark stage → cream paper → amber restaurant), not a single flat palette
Condensed, uppercase, wide-tracked labels throughout; no sentence-case microcopy in a label role
Physical-object framing: torn paper edges, a rotating stamp badge, drop shadows that read as real cast shadows on real objects
Checkerboard strip is the section-to-section thread, repeated at the top of all three sections
Motion visualizes construction (scroll-driven assembly) rather than decorating a static layout

rules.name: The Section-Owns-Its-Register Rule
rules.body: Each of the three sections has its own light/dark register (dark stage, cream paper, amber-lit restaurant); do not flatten them to one shared background color. Diner Red is the only color permitted to cross all three unchanged.

rules.name: The Rare Red Rule
rules.body: Diner Red marks category labels, prices, and thin divider rules — never a large background fill. Its scarcity is what keeps it reading as ink/stamp rather than as branding.

rules.name: The Condensed-Label Rule
rules.body: Every uppercase, wide-tracked microcopy element (category headers, captions, CTA text, stamp text) uses Barlow Condensed at 0.3em+ letter-spacing — never Anton, never the body face.

rules.name: The Matched-Media Float Rule
rules.body: Any scroll- or idle-floating element that could overlap centered text on mobile must scale its motion range down via gsap.matchMedia at the 640px boundary, not just resize the element.

rules.name: The Object-Not-Panel Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows exist to make printed/physical objects (ingredient layers, the ticket panel) feel tangible, not to indicate interactive elevation or UI hierarchy. Don't add shadow to a button or nav element to imply clickable.

rules.name: The Zero-Radius Rule
rules.body: No component in this system uses border-radius. Corners are hard because the material is paper and print stock, not soft UI chrome.

rules.name: The Torn-Edge-Is-Earned Rule
rules.body: The torn-paper edge treatment is reserved for objects standing in for physical ticket/paper stock (the menu panel). Do not apply it decoratively to unrelated UI chrome.

dos: Do keep the checkerboard strip (.bg-checker-strip, conic-gradient, 16px tile) at the top of every full-bleed section — it is the confirmed cross-section connective device, now present in all three sections per finish review.
Do pair the paper-grain noise texture (.bg-grain-paper, SVG feTurbulence) with any paper-toned or dark-stage surface that should read as physical material rather than flat digital color.
Do use Barlow Condensed at heavy letter-spacing (0.3em+) for every label/category/CTA microcopy element; reserve Anton strictly for headline-weight text.
Do keep floating/assembling ingredient imagery on a consistent shadow (drop-shadow(0 18px 28px rgba(0,0,0,0.45))) so every layer reads under one light source.

Do center burger-layer images with margin-based centering (inset-x-0 mx-auto), not translateX(-50%) — the latter was found during finish review to conflict with GSAP's own transform writes on the same element and broke the scroll-assembly end state.
donts: Don't introduce rounded corners on any panel, button, or card — this system is print/paper-derived and is hard-edged by rule (see The Zero-Radius Rule).
Don't add drop shadows to buttons or nav-style elements to signal interactivity — shadow in this system means 'physical object,' not 'clickable' (see The Object-Not-Panel Shadow Rule).

Don't use kicker/eyebrow labels (a small label sitting above a headline announcing its section). None exist in the shipped build; finish review removed them as a banned device, and this is a bare prohibition, not a canonized style.
Don't apply the torn-edge mask to anything other than genuine paper-stock objects; it is a materiality cue, not decoration.
